request: Restore soft warm-yellow city lights, the original pigeon identity with a correctly proportioned envelope, and coherent flower structure.

background.policy: Original raster is unchanged. New art is shown only through local subject masks.

method: Built-in image generation for raster edits; native SVG and CSS for subject masking and warm window light.

prompts.purpose: Original bird identity, correct envelope and flower structure
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one coherent edited illustration plate for an existing paper-theatre website, not a new design.
Input 1 is the EDIT TARGET and the strict master reference: the earliest muted matte 1672 x 941 paper-theatre scene. Input 2 is ONLY a reference for the small landscape-format envelope, NOT for its bird.

Change only the original bird's ENVELOPE and the three large pink flower heads in Input 1. The rest of the scene must keep the original pixel composition, gray-blue sky, dusty mauve curtains, muted foliage, dry fine paper grain, lighting, size and placement. No global brightening, saturation, smoothing or shiny paper.

BIRD: Keep the original pigeon itself in Input 1 exactly as it is: the exact same outline, flight posture, thin narrow overlapping wing feathers, all angular body folds, slender tapered tail strips, tiny flat dark dot eye with no highlight, slim pointed beak, dry pale neutral parchment color. Do NOT redraw it into the bird from Input 2. Do NOT enlarge its chest, thicken the feathers, round the feather ends into padded tiles, round the head, add a bead eye or peach-orange color. The bird in Input 1 is already correct. Replace only the oversized almost-square envelope under its beak with a modest horizontal rectangular cream-paper envelope, about 1.65 times as wide as tall, roughly 78 x 47 scene pixels. Its top left corner is held naturally by the existing beak tip. It hangs slightly clockwise below and to the right of the beak, visibly clear of the chest. Keep a triangular folded flap and a tiny muted dusty-rose wax seal. Borrow only the envelope's proportions and folded structure from Input 2. Bird and envelope must form one naturally connected illustrated object painted in the same original matte paper style, not pasted together. No suspension string added beyond the original string already present.

FLOWERS: repair the THREE open dusty-pink flowers at the left, right and low middle. Retain their positions, approximate outer silhouettes and the original slightly side-facing directions, sizes, muted dusty rose color, thin creased paper texture and existing stems/leaves. Redraw the internal flower structure so it reads as a coherent shallow cup made of gently overlapping broad delicate petals with a believable center. All petal bases converge toward the same center. Use a few natural unequal petal overlaps, softly curved folds and subtle center-to-edge veins. Each center should be a small low unobtrusive cluster surrounded by a loose ring of short fine curved ochre filaments with small pollen tips, with reasonable perspective and natural variation. Remove the currently weird large sculptural central mass, nested rosette shape and long comb-like radial spokes. No oversized central cone, no glowing dots, no wire firework, no perfectly repeated sunburst. The small flower must have a proportionately small center. Keep the hand-cut delicate paper illustration feeling, not a realistic photographic bloom or glossy plastic flower.

Everything else is protected: keep the entire city, sky and clouds, arches, staircase, original theatre, original box and book, floor, basket and all scenery exactly as Input 1. Do not introduce any new props, UI, captions, marks or text. Output one full-width complete 1672 x 941 scene with only these local edits.

prompts.purpose: Direct beak-envelope connection and refined proportions
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit Input 1 with only these TWO tiny corrections. Input 2 is the ORIGINAL pigeon identity reference. Keep the entire 1672 x 941 scene and the new flower petal shapes of Input 1 unchanged.

1. The pigeon in Input 1 is nearly right, but its beak has acquired an impossible thin bent hook or wire. REMOVE that bent wire completely. Restore the original short STRAIGHT triangular pointed beak from Input 2. The existing straight beak tip directly pinches the upper-left corner of the envelope, no string, no hook, no connector. Move the envelope to touch the straight beak tip naturally and make the envelope about 20 percent smaller than it currently is. The cream envelope should be a small wide rectangle, approximately 80 x 48 scene pixels, with triangular folded flap and tiny dusty-rose seal. Its top-left corner meets the beak around x915,y241. It extends to the right and slightly downward with a gentle clockwise tilt. No overlap over the bird chest. Preserve the original bird's thin feather layers, exact wings and long tail geometry, tiny flat dark dot eye, angular body and neutral matte paper. No glossy round eyeball or thick feather pads. Bird and envelope are a single physically coherent illustration.

2. Flower petals are now improved. Keep all their petal shapes and outlines. Correct ONLY the centers in the THREE pink flowers. Remove the prominent looping oval pistils and all the curled, tangled, decorative gold wire shapes. Each center should instead have a SMALL LOW subtle cluster of 3 tiny muted olive-ochre seed-like tips. Around that single center place about 12 SHORT fine mostly straight unequal soft-ochre filaments with tiny round anthers. They rise naturally from one common base, partially hidden behind the front petal. Each filament is a single simple stroke with one pollen tip: no loops, no spirals, no nested ovals, no intertwined wires, no central crown or large disk. Make the stamen ring compact and unobtrusive, hand-painted on thin matte paper with soft shadows. Keep the flowers slightly sideways as in Input 1.

Do not change anything outside the beak/envelope and the three tiny flower centers. Preserve the muted dusty palette and dry fine paper grain. No text or marks. Output one full scene.

prompts.purpose: Complete close-view flower repair to remove tangled stamens
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. This is a close view of one flower from an existing muted paper-theatre illustration. Keep the EXACT same flower shape, petals, camera, folds, paper texture, background, size and position. Only replace the incorrect golden stamen tangle at the center.

Erase ALL of the existing golden looped wire ornament, central concentric oval rings, honeycomb loops and ladder shapes. Those are anatomical mistakes, not decoration to preserve. Paint a small believable botanical center in their place: a tiny filled muted ochre cluster at the base of the flower, surrounded by about 12 independent fine filaments with tiny elongated anthers. Each filament starts at the SAME compact base and ends in ONE pollen tip. Do not connect neighboring filaments to each other. No loops anywhere, no closed outline shapes, no spirals, no ovals, no concentric rings, no knots or grid. The base is tucked partly behind the front petal. Use natural irregular lengths and oblique perspective. The new center occupies less area than the old ornament. It is a hand-painted matte paper botanical detail in subdued golden ochre, not metallic jewelry. All other pixels should stay as close to the input as possible, including petals and the surrounding scene. No text. Output this same single full flower close view with the corrected natural center.
